question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it
answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life’s guest policy allows each registered guest no more than three nights (consecutively or not) within a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Guests must stay with their resident host and carry valid ID; if staying after 10:00 PM, they need access to their approved Guest Registration email. Residents may host up to two guests at a time. Current residential students do not need guest registration. [3]

Talk with your roommate about expectations. You can contact your Resident Assistant to opt out of automatic guest registration and facilitate a roommate contract. If the contract is violated, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act. [3] A complaint about a Guide to Community Living violation should be filed with the Office of Residence Life. [22]

Overnight guests are not permitted on campus after Monday, December 14, 2026. [6]

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?
answer:
Student Accounts: If a Title IV financial aid overpayment creates a credit balance of $1.00 or greater, a refund will be issued; non-Title IV financial aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address. Checks aren’t mailed to campus mailboxes and can’t be picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

Direct deposit is optional and free. To use it, follow these steps: [1][3][4]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)
2. Locate the Student Account Info card; click on Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode, then click Verify.
5. Click the Payment Profile tab in My Profile. Edit an existing payment method or create a new one, then check the box in the Refund Option section to designate the account for direct deposit.

Direct deposit refunds are expected within one to two weeks after submitting the application. [3]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [32]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost
answer:
Public Safety handles parking permits. Apply online through the [Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [1, 7]. To complete the application [1]:
1. Log on to the RCNJ Parking Permits website, enter Permit Type, and click Continue.
2. Complete Contact Information; click Save/Update Person, then Continue.
3. Enter Vehicle Information and click Continue.
4. Review your request and click Continue.
5. Print or save the Registration Filed page with your registration request number as application verification. It is not your permit.
Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff” [1]. All students who park on campus need a current, valid permit; register each vehicle. Commuters may register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee, but only one may be parked on campus at a time [1, 6]. The permit fee is charged to your term bill, not paid when applying [7]. New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In; returning residents use their on-campus mailbox. Returning commuters pick up at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday normal operating hours, or after 3 pm at the Public Safety Main Desk if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time [1, 7].
For 2026–2027, the annual Fall/Spring permit is $250, valid through Spring 2027. Resident students pay a $50 supplement. Off-campus students are charged 7% sales tax on parking fees; on-campus students are exempt. The College does not provide a fall-only permit [7, 19].

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline [15]. The College allows a late administrative withdrawal only when extraordinary circumstances prevented you from following standard procedures, for reasons beyond your control, or you were not granted incompletes. Examples include personal illness, death or care of a terminally ill family member, catastrophic circumstances or natural disaster, or immediate employer-required relocation [16].

For an appeal, submit an appeal letter in your own words with official documentation to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular (fall or spring) semester following the term you want withdrawn. Explain the circumstances, why you could not use standard withdrawal procedures or obtain incompletes, and the term sought. If you did not apply before the semester ended, explain why. Typically, approved appeals result in W grades for all courses in one term; exceptions may be made [16].

Withdrawing may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation [11]. If dropping below full-time status, an Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be reduced or taken away; consult Financial Aid before making that change [5]. Financial Aid says withdrawing from all classes before 60% of the semester ends can require federal aid to be returned, and recommends discussing possible effects with its office [1]. SAP is reviewed annually after spring: students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits; the GPA minimum is 2.0 for undergraduates and 3.0 for graduate students [2]. The pages do not specify how a W is counted for SAP. Contact Financial Aid to discuss your award [1].

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [32]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

It depends on the course session: the full-semester withdrawal deadline has passed, but a Session II course may still be withdrawn from by its deadline above. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [7] After the refund period, there is no refund. [7]

If you withdraw by the deadline, the Registrar records a “W” on your transcript after processing the withdrawal. You can withdraw through Web Self Service; the page links to its instructions. If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email with your name, R#, CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. Instructor permission is not required, though discussing it with your professor is encouraged. [7] Withdrawal can affect financial aid eligibility, progress toward graduation, athletic compliance, housing, and campus activities. [1]

If extraordinary circumstances beyond your control prevented you from withdrawing through standard procedures, the Office of the Provost accepts applications for late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, with official documentation, by the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why you could not follow standard procedures or obtain an incomplete, and the term for which you seek withdrawal. Typically, an approved appeal results in W grades for all courses in the term. [8]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [33]
